Mike H: Heads-up — canary observed a ~2.3x tail latency regression on 2-token streaming for the FA-v2 build we pulled yesterday. Not a big throughput hit, but p99 jumps and some timeouts.
Tara L: ugh. any obvious culprit from traces?
Mike H: Preliminary perf trace points at KV cache churn + extra memcpy in the paged-attn codepath for sequences > 2048. See snippet from perf: 
```
# perf top sample
flash_attn_forward+0x34  38.2%  memcpy  21.5%  other
kv_cache_lookup 18.7%  device_memcpy_async 12.4%
```

Yu C: Interesting — did we pick up the vLLM patch that changed KV layout? I remember a layout tweak landed last week.
Sasha P: yes, vLLM merged layout-refactor (PR 321) -> changes buffer stride for paged caches. xFormers/FA builds were fine locally but our runtime kernel selection falls back to a fused variant that assumes old stride. That mismatch could cause extra copies.
Mike H: repro command I used: 
```
./run_canary --model redwood/xxx --max-seq 4096 --batch 1 --stream
```
p99: 420ms (was 180ms on previous pinned)
Tara L: can we force the non-fused kernel to confirm?
Mike H: forced to paged-nofuse and p99 returns to ~190ms. So likely fused attention variant + layout mismatch.
perf-bot: automated microbench report: 2026-03-17T15:12Z — flashattn-fused variant regression detected (p99 +115%). CI test id: perf/attn/7301
Yu C: Good catch. Two paths: 1) pin vLLM/xFormers to previous commit in canaries, 2) fix kernel selection heuristic to check KV stride compatibility before choosing fused path.
Sasha P: I prefer 2 — but need quick mitigation. Recommend pin + fast rollback of fused kernel selection in runtime until we validate layout compatibility.
Mike H: Agreed. I can push a runtime patch that adds a stride-check at init and falls back. Will also open an upstream issue on vLLM and tag xFormers/FA.
Tara L: assignable? @Yu C can you handle the upstream issue and coordinate with vendor?
Yu C: on it. I'll include a small repro and perf numbers. Planning to ask for a patch or revert of layout-refactor.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline: created canary build 2026-03-17_15_40 with runtime-stride-check -> queued for rollout.
Mike H: putting a brief note in incidents channel in case customer impact grows. So far limited to internal canaries but could hit long sequences in prod.
Sasha P: Also add an eval that exercises streaming short-burst + long-cache to catch similar regressions in future. Maybe integrate into CI perf gating.
Tara L: +1. Also add a telemetry flag to alert when memcpy% of token work > 20% for a model route.
Mike H: I'll do the runtime patch, add the telemetry, and open a PR. Short plan in PR description: "stride-compatibility check for fused attention selection; fallback to paged-nofuse on mismatch; tests + perf benchmark".
Yu C: upstream issue filed: https://github.com/vllm/vllm/issues/7890 — linked xFormers/FA maintainers and included perf log and minimal repro.
perf-bot: CI benchmark after temporary pin shows p99 restored to baseline for canary runs. perf/attn/7301 -> STATUS: mitigated.
Sasha P: thanks. once runtime change lands, we should remove the pin and re-run matrix with both fused and non-fused variants on current upstream to validate.
Mike H: I'll keep this thread updated. tl;dr: regression traced to fused-attention + vLLM KV layout change -> runtime fallback deployed as mitigation; upstream engaged. :thumbsup:
